- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Forecast mean reversion too aggressively when sentiment is volatile; model overcorrects after sharp moves.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model often misses early bearish signals and delays downward adjustments.
- High sentiment volatility correlates with higher forecast error; model struggles to adapt to rapid sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is consistently negative, model tends to forecast higher prices than true outcome — reverse the bias by adjusting downward by 1–2% of forecasted value.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates the peak — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in low-sentiment environments — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to historical mean when sentiment < -0.10.
